exposure: Mode of delivery (non-instrumental vaginal delivery, instrumental vaginal delivery, elective cesarean delivery before labor, emergency cesarean delivery during labor, unspecified cesarean delivery)
outcome: Age at attainment of pubertal milestones (Tanner stages 2-5, menarche, voice break, first ejaculation, axillary hair growth, onset of acne)
cohort: 15,731 mother-child pairs from the Danish National Birth Cohort (DNBC) with complete information on delivery mode and puberty, born between 2000 and 2003.
finding: Caesarean delivery, whether elective or emergency, was not associated with earlier pubertal timing in boys or girls.
mod_finding: Neither elective nor emergency cesarean delivery was associated with earlier age at achieving pubertal milestones in boys or girls.
followup_time: From 11 years of age until the end of puberty
